mathematics.independent_solution: Ordinary natural convection depends on buoyancy, whose effective gravitational driving is weak in an orbiting freely falling system. A fan creates circulation mechanically and brings gas into thermal contact with the instruments and shell. Microgravity does not remove molecular heat transfer and does not amplify buoyancy. Exactly C supplies the valid reason.

Weak gravity-driven buoyancy makes natural circulation weak. Mechanical gas flow past the instruments and toward the shell provides heat transport without requiring substantial buoyancy.
Reduced effective gravity weakens rather than strengthens buoyancy. The fan establishes heat-removing circulation, rather than suppressing an excessive buoyant rise and sending gas backward.

source_reviews.independent_solution: An orbiting spacecraft and its gas share approximate free fall. In its co-moving frame, effective gravity is small; ordinary buoyancy-driven free convection is consequently weak, so heating does not provide a dependable hot-gas-up/cold-gas-down circulation. A fan establishes a pressure-driven flow independently of this buoyancy mechanism, circulating gas past hot instruments to pick up thermal energy and then to the shell to transfer it. Gas still conducts heat and can undergo forced convection in weightlessness; gravitational attraction itself has not disappeared. Circulation redistributes/transports heat rather than destroying it, and does not by itself guarantee an exact fixed temperature without an external heat-loss balance.
